explain.say: In Ayemenem, a village in Kerala in south-west India, monsoon rain falls on an old house where twins, Estha and Rahel, once lived. Arundhati Roy's first novel, published in 1997, won the Booker Prize. A gentle note: it deals with caste violence, the death of a child and abuse. The timeline shows two layers of time: 1969 and 1993.

explain.say: Here is the family web. The twins' mother Ammu, divorced and treated as a disgrace, falls in love with Velutha, a gifted carpenter and the twins' friend. But Velutha is a Paravan, a caste then treated as untouchable, today called Dalit. Their love breaks what Roy calls the Love Laws: rules about who may be loved, and how much. Who will the family punish?

explain.say: Look at that week in December 1969. The twins and their English cousin Sophie Mol cross the river in a small boat; it overturns and Sophie drowns. Baby Kochamma, a bitter great-aunt, falsely accuses Velutha, and the police beat him so badly that he dies. The local Communist leader will not protect him. Who is really to blame?

events.ask: Why is The God of Small Things told out of order?

explain.say: The title sets two worlds side by side. On the left, Big Things: history, caste, politics. On the right, Small Things: a plastic hairclip, a boat, the twins' private wordplay, a few nights of love. Velutha, Roy suggests, is the God of Small Things, and the Big Things crush him. Which side does the novel make you care about?

right.title: Small Things
points: A hairclip, a boat, a moth

explain.say: Why tell it out of order? Roy reveals the drowning early and makes you wait for the causes, so you read with dread rather than suspense. The novel ends not with the tragedy but with Ammu and Velutha's love, and a promise of tomorrow. Beautiful work. Challenge: find one small object in the novel and trace how it keeps returning.

faq.q: What are the Love Laws in The God of Small Things?
faq.a: Roy's name for the unwritten rules, shaped by caste, class and gender, that decide who may love whom, and how much. Ammu and Velutha break them, and the family and state punish them savagely.
Because he is a Dalit man who loved an upper-caste woman. After Sophie Mol's death, Baby Kochamma falsely accuses him, and the police, with no one willing to defend him, beat him to death.

faq.q: Why is The God of Small Things told out of order?
faq.a: Roy moves between 1969 and 1993 so that we know the outcome early and piece together how it happened. This mirrors how trauma returns in memory and makes the small details glow.

faq.a: The twins' half-English cousin, daughter of their uncle Chacko and his English ex-wife Margaret. Her visit at Christmas 1969 and her drowning set off the tragedy.
The twins' bitter great-aunt, who resents Ammu and her children. To protect the family's name, she lies to the police about Velutha and forces the twins to confirm her story.

facts: The God of Small Things won the Booker Prize in 1997; it was Arundhati Roy's first novel.
It is set in Ayemenem, Kerala, in 1969 and 1993.
Estha and Rahel are two-egg, or dizygotic, twins.
